name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Jasmine Clark's large fundraising and outside spending advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 97%
Open seat with no polling available
model.rationale: The district's D+21 lean and the Democratic nominee's dominant financial position, with over $4 million in outside support and no outside opposition, point to a comfortable Democratic hold. Markets price a Democratic win at 97%, consistent with a Safe D rating despite the absence of polls.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a closer race or unexpected Republican outside spending would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 13th District is a heavily Democratic Atlanta-area seat, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward Democrats. David Scott's retirement created an open seat, and Democrat Jasmine Clark emerged from a competitive primary. She enters the general election with a major financial edge, having raised over $1.6 million and benefited from more than $4 million in outside support, while Republican Jonathan Chavez has reported little visible fundraising or outside backing.

No public general-election polling exists for this race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97%. The combination of the district's strong lean and Clark's resource advantage makes this a Safe Democratic seat, with the main uncertainty being the lack of direct polling data.
